exercise.name: Barbell Elevated Heel Squat
aliases: Barbell squat on a heel wedge

reference.title: Barbell Elevated Heel Squat
reference.listing: Video (title and product number from the listing URL; the page itself could not be read from this environment, so the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)

breathing.pattern: Breathe in and brace at the top, hold it down and through the bottom, breathe out as you pass the hardest part of the rise.
breathing.cadence: About 2 s down, a short pause, about 1.2 s up

prescription.load: Barbell load is user-chosen: start lighter than your normal back squat; leave about 2-3 reps in reserve (RPE 7-8).
prescription.progression: Add 2.5 kg when every rep reaches full depth with the heels down on the block.

cues.text: Bar on the upper traps just below the bony bump at the base of the neck, hands just outside the shoulders, elbows down, shoulder blades squeezed together. Heels on a low block (plates or a wedge), balls of the feet on the floor, feet about hip width, toes nearly straight.
Brace and sit straight down: knees travel well forward over the toes, trunk stays upright.
Hips below the knees, heels pressed into the block, back flat.
Drive up through the whole foot, chest leading; breathe out as you pass the hardest part.

mistakes.fix: Set the block under the heels with the balls of the feet on the floor, and press the heels down all rep.
Push the knees out over the toes.

mistakes.mistake: Rounding the lower back at depth
mistakes.fix: Stop just above the depth where the pelvis tucks under.
Pause briefly and rise under control.

kinematics.norm: A heel lift reduces the ankle dorsiflexion needed and lets the trunk stay more upright (Straub 2024)
About hip width with the toes nearly straight (Lorenzetti 2018)
Full depth, about 120 degrees or more (Straub 2024)
Less hip flexion for the same depth than with the heels flat (Straub 2024)
More upright than a flat-footed high-bar squat (Larsen 2021)
Controlled, about 2 s down and 1-1.5 s up (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual, Barbell Elevated Heel Squat, video (movement reference only)
Straub and Powers 2024, a biomechanical review of the squat exercise: implications for clinical practice (Int J Sports Phys Ther)
Lorenzetti et al. 2018, how to squat: stance widths, foot angles and experience (BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil)
Larsen et al. 2021, stance width and bar placement in back squats: kinematics, kinetics and EMG (Front Sports Act Living)

cautions: Squat inside a rack with the safety arms set just below your bottom position, or with a spotter; the rack drawn here shows only the J-hooks.
Use a stable block that cannot tip or slide (stacked plates or a squat wedge).
The forward knee travel loads the front of the knee: build depth and load gradually.
Keep the bar on the muscle of the upper back, never on the neck.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness, tingling or giving-way occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Knee pain: reduce depth or lower the block.
Balance issues: lighter bar, slower descent.

muscleNotes.quads_l: Raised heels let the knees travel far forward with an upright trunk, which shifts the work toward the knee extensors (Straub 2024).
